rounds.text: Beryl Drugs Ltd is significantly undervalued by the market, trading at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.10x against a sector benchmark of 4.03x [E2, E7]. The company's valuation is further decoupled from its underlying asset and cash efficiency when looking at its EV/EBITDA of 5.34x, which sits favorably well below the sector benchmark of 16.25x [E11]. Fundamental value is underscored by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 34 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 35.9% relative to the current market price of Rs 21.5 [E43, E44]. Furthermore, long-term profit growth has been exceptionally strong with a 5-year compounded profit growth of 44%, vastly outpacing the 5-year compounded share price growth of 18% [E19, E23]. Operational efficiency has also seen sharp improvements, highlighted by debtor days tightening from 79.1 to 39.5 days and operating cash flow reaching Rs 3.65 Cr in Mar 2026, which represents 157% of operating profit [E35, E37, E59]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the 3-year period is -10% and the trailing twelve months profit growth sits at -28% [E16, E21].
